# v0.17.3: the reasons the Brain gives for an activation that can never be accepted.
#
# Both halves of the system read this file. The server (server/brain/network.py) sets
# these slugs on a NetworkError; the phone (core/BrainAnswer.kt) treats exactly these as
# TERMINAL_REJECT and everything else - a rate limit, an internal fault, an unreachable
# server, a reason a newer Brain invented - as RETRYABLE_FAILURE.
#
# Why a file rather than two lists. v0.16.3 shipped a Kotlin/Python canonical-form
# mismatch that neither side's green suite could see, because two independent
# implementations of one rule are each self-consistent and never meet. If either side of
# this list drifts, one of the two tests reading this file fails.
#
# Adding a slug here is a decision with a cost: it lets a phone throw away a provider's
# acceptance. Retrying a settled activation costs one idempotent request; discarding a
# live one costs a buyer waiting for ever on somebody who already agreed. When in doubt,
# leave it out and let it retry.
#
# One slug per line. Blank lines and lines starting with # are ignored.

ACTIVATION_UNKNOWN
ACTIVATION_NOT_YOURS
ACTIVATION_SETTLED
ACTIVATION_EXPIRED
